# A Light at Reedbank — Opening Adventures

Original fantasy dialogue. Scripture remains in scripture.md, unchanged. These optional conversations never gate travel.

## reedbank-aunt · Aunt Nessa · The wick and the road

Nessa ties a fresh wick with blue thread. “For the wayfarers’ lantern. Their camp is beside Woodland Road; take the north-bank path into Woodland Road, then cross the timber bridge.” Outside, a fiddle is trying to keep pace with three laughing children.

“The Book’s open by the door if you want a passage for the road. Take your time. There will still be oatcakes when you get back.”

#### Success

She tucks the wick into your satchel. “Nothing grand. Just a kindness somebody needs.” The south door opens onto the landing; follow the boardwalk east, then the bank path north to Woodland Road.

#### Short

“A wick for the elven wayfarers. South door, then east along the boards and north up the bank. Oatcakes when you return.”

## reedbank-festival · Tobin · A festival worth lingering over

Tobin balances a tray of honey cakes beside the bunting. “You’re off already? The boat race hasn’t started!” A cheer travels along the docks; somebody has launched a very determined washbasin.

“You can walk to the elves. Follow the boards east, then take the bank path uphill. No swimming required.”

#### Success

He sets aside a cake. “For the walk home. If I don’t eat it first.” Across the river, lanterns swing over a second gathering. The village is wider than this one landing.

#### Short

“Follow the boards east, then the bank path uphill. I’ll save a cake. Probably.”

## woodland-elven-wayfarer · Maerin · Beyond the bend

You hear a kettle before you see the camp. Two travelers have hung their cloaks between the birches; a small lantern waits beside a coil of rope. The taller elf looks up from mending a boot.

“A Reedbank wick! Nessa remembers everything.” Maerin smiles. “I tried to repair ours with the wrong kind of rush. Being old is no protection against being foolish.”

#### Success

“We’re all creatures of Christ, the Maker of these woods. Whatever wisdom we have is received.” He settles the new wick into the lantern. “The Book is worth knowing on a quiet day, too. Remembered words can help us act with courage; a stumble in remembering does not tell us the strength of somebody’s faith.”

Farther north, a bell sounds through the trees. “Whiteledge, up on the terraces. The statuesque elves keep their record-house there. Beyond them are the Carvers’ treehouses, then Greenwood’s watch-ring. There is trouble with the road records. Follow the golden road—or sit with us a while.”

#### Short

“Thank you for the wick! Whiteledge and the Carvers’ treehouses lie north, before Greenwood. We’re fellow creatures under Christ, and glad of a neighbor’s kindness. Sit a while, or follow the north road.”

## reedbank-dockkeeper · Bram · The landing

Bram kneels beside a little boat, fitting a new oarlock. “Mind the rails. The current is lively this morning.” He points east along the boards. “Woodland Road is on this bank. No fare and no boat needed. Come back for the lantern race tonight.”

#### Success

He watches a little boat shear across the river. “That one can turn before a reed has time to bend. Iven built her after the old ferry missed its second crossing.” He leans over to retie a mooring. “East along the boards for the walking road. Keep out of the race, unless you mean to win it.”

#### Short

“Take the boardwalk east, then the bank path north. Iven’s fast boat leaves from the far dock if you want Thornwake.”

## reedbank-leaf-race · Pella · Admiral of the leaf boats

“That one is mine!” Pella points at a leaf disappearing below the landing. “It is carrying a very important ant.” She squints upstream. “I think.” The music starts again, and she skips back toward the cakes.

#### Success

Pella kneels at the edge of the boards and sets a second leaf afloat. A small black ant climbs to its highest point. “There,” she says. “Now he has a fleet.”

#### Short

“My leaf is winning! Unless that one is mine. Have you seen a very important ant?”

## woodland-second-elf · Ithren · A guest at the fire

Ithren lifts the kettle clear of the coals. His other hand keeps a loose page from blowing away: an arch, drawn twice, once standing and once broken.

“I copied the lower stones before the flood. Someone has rubbed the maker’s mark off the upper ones.”

#### Success

He turns the page. A small winged shape is caught in the edge of the drawing. “I thought it was part of the carving until it moved. Aerin at Whiteledge calls them greywings.”

He pours another cup. “North for the elven halls and the records. East for Greenwood and the old watch-ring. I am waiting for a messenger who should have crossed before noon.”

#### Short

“North goes to Whiteledge’s elven halls; east goes to Greenwood. A messenger is overdue. Ask Aerin at Whiteledge about the greywings.”
